stops.name: Beersheba, the command, the saddling of the ass
stops.campa: God tests Abraham. Abraham, He calls. Behold, here I am. Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah, and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of. Abraham rises early in the morning, saddles his ass, splits the wood for the offering, takes two young men and Isaac his son, and sets out toward the place God has told him. He says nothing. In the Quran the son himself, shown the dream, answers: Do as thou art commanded.
stops.quote: Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering.

stops.name: The road to Moriah, the third day, the two who go on alone
stops.campa: Three days they travel. On the third day Abraham lifts his eyes and sees the place afar off. He tells the young men: Abide ye here with the ass; I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you. He lays the wood of the burnt offering upon Isaac his son, and takes in his own hand the fire and the knife; and they go both of them together. And Isaac says: My father, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb? And Abraham answers: My son, God will provide himself a lamb.
stops.quote: My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.

stops.name: Mount Moriah, the altar, the knife, the ram in the thicket
stops.campa: They come to the place. Abraham builds the altar, lays the wood in order, binds Isaac his son, and lays him on the altar upon the wood. He stretches forth his hand and takes the knife to slay his son. And the angel of the Lord calls out of heaven: Abraham, Abraham! Lay not thine hand upon the lad; for now I know that thou fearest God. Abraham lifts his eyes, and behold, a ram caught in a thicket by his horns; and he offers the ram in the stead of his son. He calls the place Jehovah-jireh: the Lord will provide.
stops.quote: Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.

stops.name: Mount Moriah, the oath by Himself
stops.campa: The angel of the Lord calls to Abraham a second time out of heaven and swears the great oath, the only time God swears by Himself in all the story of the fathers. Because Abraham has done this thing and has not withheld his son, his only son, God will bless him and multiply his seed as the stars of heaven and as the sand upon the sea shore, and in his seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed. The summit of the journey: the knife lowered, the ram burning, the covenant sealed with an oath. Abraham returns to his young men, and they go together to Beersheba.
stops.quote: By myself have I sworn, saith the LORD... That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven.

stops.name: Hebron, the death of Sarah
stops.campa: Sarah lives a hundred and seven and twenty years, and dies in Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham comes to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her. Then he rises up from before his dead and speaks to the sons of Heth: I am a stranger and a sojourner with you; give me a possession of a buryingplace, that I may bury my dead out of my sight. The first death of the covenant household; the first grief; and the first need of a piece of the promised land held in the hand.
stops.quote: And Sarah died in Kirjatharba; the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.

stops.name: Hebron, the purchase of the Cave of Machpelah
stops.campa: Abraham bows to the people of the land and asks for the cave of Machpelah, at the end of Ephron's field, for the full price. Before the elders at the gate Ephron the Hittite offers it as a gift; Abraham insists on paying. He weighs out four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant. So the field and the cave and all the trees in its borders are made sure unto Abraham for a possession in the presence of the sons of Heth. There he buries Sarah his wife, the one plot of the promised land he holds outright.
stops.quote: And Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver... four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant.

stops.name: The well of Nahor / Aram-naharaim, a wife for Isaac
stops.campa: Abraham, old and well stricken in age, makes his eldest servant swear by the God of heaven not to take a wife for Isaac from the daughters of Canaan, but to go to his own country and kindred. The servant journeys to the city of Nahor in Aram-naharaim and halts by the well at evening, and prays for a sign. Before he finishes, Rebekah comes down with her pitcher, gives him drink, and waters all his camels. He knows the Lord has prospered his way, and bows his head and worships; and Rebekah goes with him to become Isaac's wife.
stops.quote: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.

stops.name: Hebron, the death of Abraham, buried by Isaac and Ishmael
stops.campa: Abraham lives a hundred and threescore and fifteen years, and gives up the ghost, and dies in a good old age, an old man and full of years, and is gathered to his people. And his sons Isaac and Ishmael, the two lines parted long ago, come together and bury him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field Abraham bought of the sons of Heth, beside Sarah his wife. The friend of God is laid in the one plot of the land he owned. His Kaaba faces Muhammad's; his Moriah faces the Temple and Golgotha; his grave is claimed by all his children.
stops.quote: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people. And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah.
